verses.1:1: Paul, a slave of Christ Jesus, a called apostle, set apart for the gospel of God,
verses.1:2: which He promised beforehand through His prophets in holy Scriptures,
verses.1:3: concerning His Son, who came from the seed of David according to the flesh,
verses.1:4: who was designated Son of God in power according to the Spirit of holiness by the resurrection of the dead, Jesus Christ our Lord,
verses.1:5: through whom we received grace and apostleship for the obedience of faith among all the nations for the sake of His name,
verses.1:6: among whom you also are those called of Jesus Christ;
verses.1:7: to all who are in Rome, beloved of God, called saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:8: First, I give thanks to my God through Jesus Christ concerning all of you, because your faith is being proclaimed in the whole world.
verses.1:9: For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the gospel of His Son, how unceasingly I make mention of you
verses.1:10: always in my prayers, asking if somehow now at last I may succeed in the will of God to come to you.
verses.1:11: For I long to see you, so that I may impart some spiritual gift to you in order that you may be established,
verses.1:12: that is, to be mutually encouraged among you through each other's faith, both yours and mine.
verses.1:13: Now I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that many times I planned to come to you, and have been prevented until now, so that I might have some fruit among you also, just as among the rest of the Gentiles.
verses.1:14: Both to Greeks and to barbarians, both to the wise and to the foolish, I am a debtor;
verses.1:15: so, as for my part, I am eager to proclaim the gospel to you also who are in Rome.
verses.1:16: For I am not ashamed of the gospel, since it is God's power for salvation to everyone who believes, both to the Jew first and to the Greek.
verses.1:17: For the righteousness of God is revealed in it from faith to faith, just as it is written, "But the righteous one will live by faith."
verses.1:18: For the wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of people who suppress the truth in unrighteousness,
verses.1:19: because what can be known about God is plain within them, for God made it plain to them.
verses.1:20: For His invisible qualities have been clearly perceived since the creation of the world, being understood by the things made—both His eternal power and divine nature—with the result that they are without excuse,
verses.1:21: because, although knowing God, they neither glorified Him as God nor gave thanks, but became futile in their reasonings, and their senseless heart was darkened.
verses.1:22: Claiming to be wise, they became fools,
verses.1:23: and exchanged the glory of the imperishable God for a likeness of an image of a perishable human being, and of birds, four-footed animals, and reptiles.
verses.1:24: Therefore God handed them over in the desires of their hearts to impurity, so that their bodies would be dishonored among themselves,
verses.1:25: since they exchanged the truth of God for the lie, and revered and served the creation rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen.
verses.1:26: Because of this, God handed them over to passions of dishonor; for their females exchanged the natural function for that which is contrary to nature,
verses.1:27: and likewise also the males, having abandoned the natural function of the female, burned in their craving toward one another, males with males working out indecency and receiving in themselves the due penalty of their error.
verses.1:28: And just as they did not see fit to keep God in their knowledge, God handed them over to a depraved mind, to do things that are not fitting,
verses.1:29: having been filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, greed, malice; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, evil-mindedness; whisperers,
verses.1:30: slanderers, God-haters, insolent, haughty, braggarts, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,
verses.1:31: senseless, untrustworthy, without natural affection, merciless;
verses.1:32: who, although fully knowing the righteous decree of God, that those who practice such things are worthy of death, not only do them, but also give approval to those who practice them.
verses.2:1: Therefore you are without excuse, O man, everyone who judges; for in that which you judge the other person, you condemn yourself, because you who judge practice the very same things.
verses.2:2: Now we know that the judgment of God is according to truth upon those who practice such things.
verses.2:3: And do you suppose this, O man, you who judge those who practice such things and yet do them yourself, that you will escape the judgment of God?
verses.2:4: Or do you despise the wealth of His kindness and forbearance and patience, not knowing that the kindness of God is leading you to repentance?
verses.2:5: But according to your hardness and unrepentant heart, you are storing up wrath for yourself in the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God,
verses.2:6: who will repay each person according to his deeds:
verses.2:7: to those who by endurance in good work seek glory and honor and imperishability, eternal life;
verses.2:8: but to those who are driven by selfish ambition and disobey the truth, yet obey unrighteousness, wrath and fury,
verses.2:9: affliction and distress upon every human soul who carries out what is evil, both of the Jew first and of the Greek;
verses.2:10: but glory and honor and peace to everyone who works what is good, both to the Jew first and to the Greek.
verses.2:11: For there is no favoritism with God.
verses.2:12: For as many as sinned without law will also perish without law, and as many as sinned under law will be judged through law;
verses.2:13: for the hearers of the law are not righteous before God, but the doers of the law will be justified.
verses.2:14: For whenever Gentiles, who do not have the law, do by nature the things of the law, these, though not having the law, are a law to themselves,
verses.2:15: since they show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience bearing witness along with it, and between one another their thoughts accusing or even defending them,
verses.2:16: on the day when God judges the hidden things of people, according to my gospel, through Christ Jesus.
verses.2:17: Now if you bear the name Jew, and rely on the law, and boast in God,
verses.2:18: and know His will, and approve the things that are superior, being instructed from the law,
verses.2:19: and are confident that you yourself are a guide of the blind, a light to those in darkness,
verses.2:20: an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of infants, having the embodiment of knowledge and of the truth in the law—
verses.2:21: you, therefore, who teach another, do you not teach yourself? You who preach not to steal, do you steal?
verses.2:22: You who say not to commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?
verses.2:23: You who boast in the law, through the transgression of the law do you dishonor God?
verses.2:24: For "the name of God is blasphemed among the Gentiles because of you," just as it is written.
verses.2:25: For circumcision indeed benefits if you practice the law; but if you are a transgressor of the law, your circumcision has become uncircumcision.
verses.2:26: If, therefore, the uncircumcised person keeps the righteous decrees of the law, will not his uncircumcision be counted as circumcision?
verses.2:27: And the uncircumcised by nature who fulfills the law will judge you who, with the written letter and circumcision, are a transgressor of the law.
verses.2:28: For a Jew is not the one who is so outwardly, nor is circumcision what is outward in the flesh;
verses.2:29: rather, a Jew is the one who is so inwardly, and circumcision is of the heart, by the Spirit, not by the letter; his praise is not from people, but from God.
verses.3:1: What then is the advantage of the Jew, or what is the benefit of circumcision?
verses.3:2: Much in every way. For first of all, they were entrusted with the oracles of God.
verses.3:3: What then? If some proved unfaithful, will their unfaithfulness nullify the faithfulness of God?
verses.3:4: May it never happen! Rather, let God prove true, and every person a liar, just as it is written: "So that You may be justified in Your words and will prevail when You are judged."
verses.3:5: But if our unrighteousness establishes God's righteousness, what shall we say? God, who brings wrath, is not unrighteous, is He? I am speaking in human terms.
verses.3:6: May it never happen! For otherwise, how will God judge the world?
verses.3:7: But if through my falsehood the truth of God abounded to His glory, why am I too still being judged as a sinner,
verses.3:8: and why not—just as we are slandered and just as some claim we say—"Let us do evil so that good may come"? Their judgment is deserved.
verses.3:9: What then? Are we at an advantage? Not at all, for we have already charged that both Jews and Greeks are all under sin,
verses.3:10: just as it is written: "There is no righteous person, not even one;
verses.3:11: there is no one who understands, there is no one who seeks out God;
verses.3:12: all have turned away; together they have become worthless; there is no one doing good, not even a single one.
verses.3:13: Their throat is an open tomb; with their tongues they kept deceiving; the venom of asps is under their lips;
verses.3:14: whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness;
verses.3:15: their feet are quick to shed blood;
verses.3:16: ruin and misery lie in their paths,
verses.3:17: and they have not known the path of peace.
verses.3:18: No fear of God is before their eyes."
verses.3:19: Now we know that whatever the law says, it speaks to those in the law, so that every mouth may be silenced and the entire world may become accountable to God;
verses.3:20: because by works of the law no flesh will be justified before Him, for through the law comes the recognition of sin.
verses.3:21: But now, apart from the law, a righteousness of God has been manifested, attested by the Law and the Prophets,
verses.3:22: namely, the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe. For there is no distinction;
verses.3:23: for all sinned and fall short of the glory of God,
verses.3:24: being justified freely by His grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus,
verses.3:25: whom God presented publicly as a propitiation through faith, by His blood, as a demonstration of His righteousness, because of the passing over of the sins previously committed
verses.3:26: in the forbearance of God, for the demonstration of His righteousness at the present time, so that He might be righteous and the One who justifies the one who has faith in Jesus.
verses.3:27: Where then is boasting? It has been shut out. Through what kind of law? That of works? No, rather through a law of faith.
verses.3:28: For we conclude that a person is justified by faith apart from works of the law.
verses.3:29: Or is God the God of Jews only? Is He not of Gentiles also? Yes, of Gentiles also,
verses.3:30: since indeed there is one God, who will justify the circumcised by faith and the uncircumcised through faith.
verses.3:31: Do we then nullify the law through faith? May it never happen! On the contrary, we establish the law.
verses.4:1: What then shall we say that Abraham, our forefather according to the flesh, has found?
verses.4:2: For if Abraham was justified by works, he has ground for boasting, yet not before God.
verses.4:3: For what does the Scripture say? "And Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him for righteousness."
verses.4:4: Now to the one who works, the wage is not credited according to grace, but according to obligation;
verses.4:5: but to the one who does not work, yet believes in the One who justifies the ungodly, his faith is credited for righteousness,
verses.4:6: just as David also speaks of the blessedness of the person to whom God credits righteousness apart from works:
verses.4:7: "Blessed are those whose lawless acts have been forgiven, and whose sins have been covered;
verses.4:8: blessed is the man to whom the Lord will certainly not credit sin."
verses.4:9: Is this blessedness then upon the circumcised, or also upon the uncircumcised? For we say: "Faith was credited to Abraham for righteousness."
verses.4:10: How then was it credited? When he was circumcised, or when uncircumcised? Not when circumcised, but when uncircumcised;
verses.4:11: and he received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness of the faith he had while uncircumcised, so that he would be the father of all who believe while uncircumcised, in order that righteousness would be credited to them,
verses.4:12: and the father of the circumcised, for those who are not merely of the circumcision, but who also walk in the footsteps of the faith that our father Abraham had while uncircumcised.
verses.4:13: For the promise to Abraham or to his offspring, that he would be heir of the world, was not through the law, but through the righteousness of faith.
verses.4:14: For if those who are of the law are heirs, faith has been made empty and the promise has been nullified;
verses.4:15: for the law produces wrath; yet where there is no law, neither is there transgression.
verses.4:16: For this reason it is by faith, so that it may be according to grace, in order that the promise may be certain to all the offspring, not only to those who are of the law, but also to those who are of the faith of Abraham (who is the father of us all,
verses.4:17: just as it is written: "I have appointed you the father of many nations"), in the presence of the God in whom he believed, who gives life to the dead and calls the things that do not exist as though they exist.
verses.4:18: Contrary to hope, in hope he believed, so that he would become the father of many nations, according to what had been spoken: "So will your offspring be."
verses.4:19: And without growing weak in faith, he considered his own body, already deadened—being about a hundred years old—and the deadness of Sarah's womb;
verses.4:20: yet regarding the promise of God he did not waver in unbelief, but was strengthened in faith, giving glory to God
verses.4:21: and being fully convinced that what He has promised, He is also able to perform.
verses.4:22: Therefore it was also credited to him for righteousness.
verses.4:23: Now it was not written for his sake alone that it was credited to him,
verses.4:24: but also for our sake, to whom it will be credited—those who believe in the One who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead,
verses.4:25: who was handed over because of our trespasses and was raised for our justification.
verses.5:1: Having been justified, therefore, by faith, let us have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.5:2: through whom we have also obtained access by faith into this grace in which we stand; and we boast in the hope of the glory of God.
verses.5:3: And not only that, but we also boast in our afflictions, knowing that affliction produces endurance,
verses.5:4: and endurance, proven character; and proven character, hope.
verses.5:5: And hope does not put to shame, because the love of God has been poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us.
verses.5:6: For while we were still weak, at the appointed time Christ died for the ungodly.
verses.5:7: For scarcely will anyone die for a righteous person, though perhaps for a good person someone might even dare to die.
verses.5:8: But God proves His own love toward us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
verses.5:9: Much more then, having now been justified by His blood, we shall be saved through Him from the wrath.
verses.5:10: For if while we were enemies we were reconciled to God through the death of His Son, much more, having been reconciled, we shall be saved by His life.
verses.5:11: And not only that, but we are also boasting in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received the reconciliation.
verses.5:12: For this reason, just as sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, in this way death also spread to all people, because all sinned—
verses.5:13: for until the law sin was in the world, yet sin is not charged to account where there is no law.
verses.5:14: Nevertheless, death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who had not sinned in the likeness of Adam's transgression, who is a type of the One who was to come.
verses.5:15: Yet the gracious gift is not like the trespass. For if by the trespass of the one the many died, much more did the grace of God and the gift by the grace of the one man, Jesus Christ, abound to the many.
verses.5:16: And the gift is not like what came through the one who sinned; for the judgment arose from one, leading to condemnation, whereas the gracious gift arose from many trespasses, leading to justification.
verses.5:17: For if by the trespass of the one, death reigned through the one, much more will those who receive the abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one, Jesus Christ.
verses.5:18: So then, as through one trespass the result for all people was condemnation, so also through one act of righteousness the result for all people is justification of life.
verses.5:19: For just as through the disobedience of the one man the many were made sinners, so also through the obedience of the One the many will be made righteous.
verses.5:20: Now the law came in alongside so that the trespass might increase; yet where sin increased, grace abounded all the more,
verses.5:21: so that just as sin reigned in death, so also grace might reign through righteousness leading to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
verses.6:1: What then shall we say? Should we continue in sin so that grace may increase?
verses.6:2: May it never happen! How shall we who died to sin still live in it?
verses.6:3: Or are you unaware that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into His death?
verses.6:4: We were buried with Him, therefore, through baptism into death, so that just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we too might walk in newness of life.
verses.6:5: For if we have become united with the likeness of His death, we shall certainly also be united with the likeness of His resurrection,
verses.6:6: knowing this, that our old self was crucified with Him, so that the body of sin might be rendered powerless, in order that we would no longer be enslaved to sin;
verses.6:7: for the one who has died has been acquitted from sin.
verses.6:8: Now if we died with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with Him,
verses.6:9: knowing that Christ, having been raised from the dead, dies no more; death no longer has dominion over Him.
verses.6:10: For the death He died, He died to sin once for all; but the life He lives, He lives to God.
verses.6:11: So you also, consider yourselves to be dead to sin, yet alive to God in Christ Jesus.
verses.6:12: Therefore do not let sin reign in your mortal body so as to obey its desires,
verses.6:13: and do not go on presenting your members to sin as weapons of unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as those alive from the dead, and your members to God as weapons of righteousness.
verses.6:14: For sin will not have dominion over you, because you are not under law, but under grace.
verses.6:15: What then? Should we sin because we are not under law, but under grace? May it never happen!
verses.6:16: Do you not know that to whomever you present yourselves as slaves for obedience, you are slaves of the one whom you obey, either of sin leading to death, or of obedience leading to righteousness?
verses.6:17: But thanks be to God that though you were slaves of sin, you obeyed from the heart that pattern of teaching to which you were committed,
verses.6:18: and having been set free from sin, you became enslaved to righteousness.
verses.6:19: I am speaking in human terms because of the weakness of your flesh. For just as you presented your members as slaves to impurity and to lawlessness leading to lawlessness, so now present your members as slaves to righteousness leading to sanctification.
verses.6:20: For when you were slaves of sin, you were free with respect to righteousness.
verses.6:21: What fruit, then, did you have at that time from the things of which you are now ashamed? For the end of those things is death.
verses.6:22: But now, having been set free from sin and having been enslaved to God, you have your fruit leading to sanctification, and the end, eternal life.
verses.6:23: For the wages of sin is death, whereas the gracious gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
verses.7:1: Or are you unaware, brothers—for I am speaking to those who know the law—that the law has dominion over a person for as long as he lives?
verses.7:2: For a married woman is bound by law to her living husband; but if her husband dies, she is released from the law concerning her husband.
verses.7:3: So then, while her husband is living, she will be called an adulteress if she belongs to another man; yet if her husband dies, she is free from that law, so that she is not an adulteress if she belongs to another man.
verses.7:4: Therefore, my brothers, you also were put to death to the law through the body of Christ, so that you might belong to another—to Him who was raised from the dead—in order that we might bear fruit for God.
verses.7:5: For when we were in the flesh, the sinful passions that were through the law were at work in our members so as to bear fruit for death.
verses.7:6: But now we have been released from the law, having died to that in which we were held captive, so that we serve in newness of the Spirit and not in oldness of the letter.
verses.7:7: What then shall we say? Is the law sin? May it never happen! On the contrary, I would not have come to know sin except through the law; for I would not have known coveting either if the law had not said, "You shall not covet."
verses.7:8: But sin, seizing an opportunity through the commandment, produced in me every kind of coveting; for apart from law, sin is dead.
verses.7:9: Now I was once alive apart from law; yet when the commandment came, sin came back to life,
verses.7:10: and I died; and the very commandment that was for life was found to bring death to me.
verses.7:11: For sin, seizing an opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through it killed me.
verses.7:12: So then, the law is holy, and the commandment is holy and righteous and good.
verses.7:13: Did what is good, then, become death to me? May it never happen! Rather, it was sin—so that it might be shown to be sin by producing death in me through what is good—so that through the commandment sin might become sinful beyond measure.
verses.7:14: For we know that the law is spiritual, whereas I am of flesh, sold under sin.
verses.7:15: For what I am carrying out, I do not understand; for I do not practice what I want to do, but what I hate, that I do.
verses.7:16: Now if I do the very thing I do not want, I agree with the law, that it is good.
verses.7:17: So now it is no longer I who carry it out, but sin that dwells in me.
verses.7:18: For I know that nothing good dwells in me, that is, in my flesh; for the willing is present with me, yet the carrying out of what is good is not.
verses.7:19: For the good that I want, I do not do; instead, the evil that I do not want, this I practice.
verses.7:20: Now if I do the very thing I do not want, it is no longer I who carry it out, but sin that dwells in me.
verses.7:21: I find, therefore, this law: when I want to do what is good, evil is present with me.
verses.7:22: For I delight in the law of God in my inner self,
verses.7:23: yet I see a different law in my members, waging war against the law of my mind and making me a captive to the law of sin that is in my members.
verses.7:24: What a wretched person I am! Who will rescue me from this body of death?
verses.7:25: Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord! So then, I myself with my mind serve the law of God, yet with my flesh, the law of sin.
verses.8:1: So then, there is now no condemnation for those in Christ Jesus.
verses.8:2: For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has freed you from the law of sin and of death.
verses.8:3: For what was impossible for the law, in that it was weak through the flesh, God—having sent His own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and concerning sin—condemned sin in the flesh,
verses.8:4: so that the righteous requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us, who do not walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.
verses.8:5: For those who exist according to the flesh set their minds on the things of the flesh, whereas those who exist according to the Spirit set their minds on the things of the Spirit.
verses.8:6: For the mindset of the flesh is death, whereas the mindset of the Spirit is life and peace;
verses.8:7: because the mindset of the flesh is hostility toward God, for it does not submit itself to the law of God, nor indeed is it able to;
verses.8:8: and those who are in the flesh are not able to please God.
verses.8:9: You, however, are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit, if indeed the Spirit of God dwells in you. Yet if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, this person does not belong to Him.
verses.8:10: And if Christ is in you, though the body is dead because of sin, the spirit is life because of righteousness.
verses.8:11: Yet if the Spirit of Him who raised Jesus from the dead dwells in you, He who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also make your mortal bodies alive through His Spirit who dwells in you.
verses.8:12: So then, brothers, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live according to the flesh;
verses.8:13: for if you live according to the flesh, you are going to die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the practices of the body, you will live.
verses.8:14: For as many as are led by the Spirit of God, these are sons of God.
verses.8:15: For you did not receive a spirit of slavery again leading to fear, but you received a Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry out, "Abba! Father!"
verses.8:16: The Spirit Himself testifies together with our spirit that we are children of God;
verses.8:17: and if children, then also heirs: heirs of God, and fellow heirs with Christ, if indeed we suffer together with Him so that we may also be glorified together with Him.
verses.8:18: For I reckon that the sufferings of the present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory that is about to be revealed to us.
verses.8:19: For the eager expectation of creation awaits the revealing of the sons of God.
verses.8:20: For creation was subjected to futility, not willingly, but because of the One who subjected it, in hope
verses.8:21: that creation itself will also be freed from its slavery to decay into the freedom of the glory of the children of God.
verses.8:22: For we know that the entire creation groans together and suffers birth pains together until now.
verses.8:23: And not only that, but we ourselves also, who have the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, eagerly awaiting adoption, the redemption of our body.
verses.8:24: For in this hope we were saved; yet hope that is seen is not hope, for who hopes for what he sees?
verses.8:25: But if we hope for what we do not see, we eagerly await it through endurance.
verses.8:26: And in the same way the Spirit also comes alongside to help our weakness; for we do not know what we should pray for as we ought, but the Spirit Himself intercedes with unspoken groanings;
verses.8:27: and He who searches the hearts knows what the mindset of the Spirit is, because He intercedes for the saints according to God.
verses.8:28: Now we know that all things work together toward good for those who love God, for those who are called according to His purpose.
verses.8:29: Because those whom He foreknew, He also predestined to be conformed to the image of His Son, so that He would be the firstborn among many brothers;
verses.8:30: and those whom He predestined, these He also called; and those whom He called, these He also justified; and those whom He justified, these He also glorified.
verses.8:31: What then shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who is against us?
verses.8:32: He who indeed did not spare His own Son, but handed Him over on behalf of us all, how will He not also with Him graciously give us all things?
verses.8:33: Who will bring an accusation against God's chosen ones? God is the One who justifies.
verses.8:34: Who is the one who condemns? Christ Jesus is the One who died—even more, who was raised—who is also at the right hand of God, who also intercedes on our behalf.
verses.8:35: Who will separate us from the love of Christ? Affliction, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or danger, or sword?
verses.8:36: Just as it is written, "For Your sake we are being put to death all day long; we were reckoned as sheep for slaughter."
verses.8:37: Yet in all these things we triumph completely through Him who loved us.
verses.8:38: For I am convinced that neither death nor life, nor angels nor rulers, nor things present nor things to come, nor powers,
verses.8:39: nor height nor depth, nor any other creature will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
verses.9:1: I speak the truth in Christ; I am not lying, as my conscience bears witness with me in the Holy Spirit,
verses.9:2: that I have great grief and continual anguish in my heart.
verses.9:3: For I could wish that I myself were accursed, cut off from Christ, for the sake of my brothers, my relatives according to the flesh,
verses.9:4: who are Israelites, to whom belong the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the sacred service, and the promises;
verses.9:5: to whom belong the fathers, and from whom comes the Christ according to the flesh, who is over all, God blessed forever. Amen.
verses.9:6: Yet it is not as though the word of God has failed. For not all who are from Israel are Israel;
verses.9:7: nor are all children because they are Abraham's offspring; rather, "In Isaac your offspring will be named."
verses.9:8: That is, the children of the flesh are not the ones who are children of God, but the children of the promise are counted as offspring.
verses.9:9: For this is a word of promise: "At this time I will come, and Sarah will have a son."
verses.9:10: And not only this, but also Rebekah, having conceived by one man, our father Isaac—
verses.9:11: for when they were not yet born and had done nothing good or bad, so that God's purpose according to election might remain,
verses.9:12: not from works but from Him who calls—it was said to her, "The older will serve the younger,"
verses.9:13: just as it is written: "Jacob I loved, yet Esau I hated."
verses.9:14: What then shall we say? Is there unrighteousness with God? May it never happen!
verses.9:15: For He says to Moses, "I will have mercy on whomever I have mercy, and I will show compassion to whomever I show compassion."
verses.9:16: So then, it is not of the one who wills nor of the one who runs, but of God who shows mercy.
verses.9:17: For the Scripture says to Pharaoh, "For this very purpose I raised you up, so that I might display My power in you, and so that My name might be declared throughout all the earth."
verses.9:18: So then, He shows mercy to whom He wills, and He hardens whom He wills.
verses.9:19: You will say to me then, "Why then does He still find fault? For who has resisted His will?"
verses.9:20: Indeed, who are you, O human, who talks back to God? Will what is molded say to the one who molded it, "Why did you make me like this?"
verses.9:21: Or does the potter not have authority over the clay, to make from the same lump one vessel for honor and another for dishonor?
verses.9:22: And what if God, desiring to display wrath and to make His power known, bore with much patience vessels of wrath fitted for destruction,
verses.9:23: and in order to make known the riches of His glory upon vessels of mercy, which He prepared beforehand for glory—
verses.9:24: us whom He also called, not only from the Jews, but also from the Gentiles?
verses.9:25: As He also says in Hosea, "I will call those who were not My people, 'My people,' and her who was not loved, 'Beloved';
verses.9:26: and it will be that in the place where it was said to them, 'You are not My people,' there they will be called sons of the living God."
verses.9:27: And Isaiah cries out concerning Israel: "Though the number of the sons of Israel be like the sand of the sea, the remnant will be saved;
verses.9:28: for the Lord will execute His word upon the earth, completing and cutting it short."
verses.9:29: And just as Isaiah said beforehand: "If the Lord of Sabaoth had not left us offspring, we would have become like Sodom, and we would have been made like Gomorrah."
verses.9:30: What then shall we say? That Gentiles who were not pursuing righteousness attained righteousness, namely, the righteousness that is from faith;
verses.9:31: but Israel, pursuing a law of righteousness, did not arrive at the law.
verses.9:32: Why? Because it was not from faith, but as if from works. They stumbled against the stone of stumbling,
verses.9:33: just as it is written: "Look, I am placing in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, and the one who believes in Him will not be put to shame."
verses.10:1: Brothers, the desire of my heart and prayer to God on their behalf is for salvation.
verses.10:2: For I bear witness concerning them that they have zeal for God, yet not according to knowledge;
verses.10:3: for, not knowing the righteousness of God and seeking to establish their own, they did not submit to the righteousness of God.
verses.10:4: For Christ is the end of the law, resulting in righteousness for everyone who believes.
verses.10:5: For Moses writes concerning the righteousness from the law, "The person who does these things will live by it."
verses.10:6: But the righteousness from faith speaks this way: "Do not say in your heart, 'Who will ascend into heaven?'" (that is, to bring Christ down),
verses.10:7: or, "Who will descend into the abyss?" (that is, to bring Christ up from the dead).
verses.10:8: Rather, what does it say? "The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart"—that is, the word of faith that we proclaim:
verses.10:9: that if with your mouth you confess Jesus as Lord, and in your heart you believe that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved;
verses.10:10: for with the heart one believes for righteousness, and with the mouth one confesses for salvation.
verses.10:11: For the Scripture says, "Anyone who believes in Him will not be put to shame."
verses.10:12: For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek, since the same One is Lord of all, rich toward all who call upon Him;
verses.10:13: for "Whoever calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved."
verses.10:14: How then are they to call upon Him in whom they have not believed? And how are they to believe in Him whom they have not heard? And how are they to hear without someone proclaiming?
verses.10:15: And how are they to proclaim unless they are sent? Just as it is written: "How beautiful are the feet of those who announce good news of good things!"
verses.10:16: Yet not all obeyed the gospel; for Isaiah says, "Lord, who has believed our report?"
verses.10:17: Therefore faith is from hearing, and hearing is through the word of Christ.
verses.10:18: But I say, did they not hear? Indeed they did: "Their voice went out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the inhabited world."
verses.10:19: But I say, did Israel not know? First Moses says, "I will provoke you to jealousy by what is not a nation; by a nation without understanding I will stir you to anger."
verses.10:20: And Isaiah is bold and says, "I was found by those who were not seeking Me; I became manifest to those who were not inquiring of Me."
verses.10:21: But concerning Israel He says, "All day long I stretched out My hands to a disobedient and contrary people."
verses.11:1: I say then, has God cast off His people? May it never happen! For I too am an Israelite, from the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
verses.11:2: God has not cast off His people whom He foreknew. Or do you not know what the Scripture says in the account of Elijah, how he appeals to God against Israel?
verses.11:3: "Lord, they have killed Your prophets, they have torn down Your altars, and I alone am left, and they are seeking my life."
verses.11:4: But what does the divine answer say to him? "I have left for Myself seven thousand men who have not bent the knee to Baal."
verses.11:5: So then, at the present time also, there has come to be a remnant according to an election of grace.
verses.11:6: But if it is by grace, it is no longer from works; otherwise grace is no longer grace.
verses.11:7: What then? What Israel is seeking, this it did not obtain, but the elect obtained it; and the rest were hardened,
verses.11:8: just as it is written: "God gave them a spirit of stupor, eyes not to see and ears not to hear, until this very day."
verses.11:9: And David says: "Let their table become a snare and a trap and a stumbling block and a repayment to them;
verses.11:10: let their eyes be darkened so as not to see, and bend their backs continually."
verses.11:11: I say then, did they stumble so that they would fall? May it never happen! Rather, by their trespass salvation has come to the Gentiles, in order to make them jealous.
verses.11:12: Now if their trespass is riches for the world, and their loss is riches for the Gentiles, how much more will their fullness be!
verses.11:13: But I am speaking to you who are Gentiles. Inasmuch then as I am an apostle of the Gentiles, I honor my ministry,
verses.11:14: if somehow I might make my own flesh jealous and save some of them.
verses.11:15: For if their rejection is the reconciliation of the world, what will their acceptance be but life from the dead?
verses.11:16: And if the firstfruits are holy, the lump is also; and if the root is holy, the branches are also.
verses.11:17: But if some of the branches were broken off, and you, being a wild olive shoot, were grafted in among them and became a fellow partaker of the root of the richness of the olive tree,
verses.11:18: do not boast over the branches; yet if you boast, it is not you who sustains the root, but the root sustains you.
verses.11:19: You will say then, "Branches were broken off so that I might be grafted in."
verses.11:20: True enough! By unbelief they were broken off, but you stand by faith. Do not be haughty, but fear;
verses.11:21: for if God did not spare the natural branches, He will not spare you either.
verses.11:22: See then the kindness and severity of God: toward those who fell, severity; but toward you, God's kindness, if you remain in that kindness; otherwise you also will be cut off.
verses.11:23: And those others also, if they do not remain in unbelief, will be grafted in; for God is able to graft them in again.
verses.11:24: For if you were cut out of what is by nature a wild olive tree, and contrary to nature were grafted into a cultivated olive tree, how much more will these natural branches be grafted into their own olive tree!
verses.11:25: For I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of this mystery, so that you will not be wise in your own estimation: that a hardening in part has come upon Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles has come in,
verses.11:26: and in this way all Israel will be saved, just as it is written: "The Deliverer will come from Zion; He will turn away ungodliness from Jacob.
verses.11:27: And this is the covenant from Me to them, when I take away their sins."
verses.11:28: With respect to the gospel, they are enemies for your sake; but with respect to election, they are beloved for the sake of the fathers.
verses.11:29: For the gracious gifts and the calling of God are irrevocable.
verses.11:30: For just as you once disobeyed God, yet have now received mercy through their disobedience,
verses.11:31: so these also have now disobeyed because of the mercy shown to you, so that they themselves may also now receive mercy.
verses.11:32: For God has confined all in disobedience, so that He may show mercy to all.
verses.11:33: Oh, the depth of the riches and wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are His judgments and untraceable His ways!
verses.11:34: For who has known the mind of the Lord, or who has become His counselor?
verses.11:35: Or who has first given to Him, and it will be repaid to him?
verses.11:36: For all things are from Him and through Him and to Him; to Him be the glory forever. Amen.
verses.12:1: Therefore I urge you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy, well-pleasing to God, which is your rational service of worship.
verses.12:2: And do not be conformed to this age, but be transformed by the renewal of the mind, so that you may test and approve what the will of God is—what is good and well-pleasing and complete.
verses.12:3: For through the grace given to me I say to every person who is among you not to think more highly than one ought to think, but to think with a view to sound judgment, just as God has apportioned to each a measure of faith.
verses.12:4: For just as in one body we have many members, and all the members do not have the same function,
verses.12:5: so we, the many, are one body in Christ, and individually members of one another.
verses.12:6: Now having gifts that differ according to the grace given to us: whether prophecy, according to the proportion of faith;
verses.12:7: or service, in serving; or the one who teaches, in teaching;
verses.12:8: or the one who encourages, in encouragement; the one who shares, with simplicity; the one who leads, with diligence; the one who shows mercy, with cheerfulness.
verses.12:9: Let love be without hypocrisy. Detest what is evil; cling to what is good.
verses.12:10: In brotherly love be tenderly devoted to one another; in honor outdo one another;
verses.12:11: in diligence not lagging behind, in spirit boiling with zeal, serving the Lord;
verses.12:12: rejoicing in hope, enduring in affliction, persevering in prayer;
verses.12:13: sharing in the needs of the saints, pursuing hospitality.
verses.12:14: Bless those who persecute; bless and do not curse.
verses.12:15: Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.
verses.12:16: Be of the same mind toward one another; do not set your mind on high things, but associate with the lowly. Do not become wise in your own estimation.
verses.12:17: Repay no one evil for evil; take thought for what is honorable in the sight of all people.
verses.12:18: If possible, so far as it depends on you, live at peace with all people.
verses.12:19: Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but give place to wrath; for it is written, "Vengeance belongs to Me; I will repay," says the Lord.
verses.12:20: Instead, "if your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink; for by doing this you will heap coals of fire upon his head."
verses.12:21: Do not be conquered by evil, but conquer evil with good.
verses.13:1: Let every person submit to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except by God, and the ones that exist have been appointed by God.
verses.13:2: Therefore, whoever resists authority has opposed the ordinance of God, and those who stand in opposition will receive judgment upon themselves.
verses.13:3: For rulers are not a source of fear to a good deed, but to an evil one. Do you want not to fear authority? Do what is good, and you will have praise from it;
verses.13:4: for it is God's servant to you for good. But if you do what is evil, be afraid; for it does not carry the sword for nothing. For it is God's servant, an avenger for wrath against the one who practices evil.
verses.13:5: Therefore it is necessary to submit, not only because of wrath, but also because of conscience.
verses.13:6: For because of this you also pay taxes, since they are ministers of God, continually devoting themselves to this very thing.
verses.13:7: Pay to all what is owed: tax to whom tax is due, toll to whom toll is due, fear to whom fear is due, honor to whom honor is due.
verses.13:8: Owe nothing to anyone except to love one another; for the one who loves another has fulfilled the law.
verses.13:9: For the commands, "You shall not commit adultery, you shall not murder, you shall not steal, you shall not covet," and any other commandment there may be, are summed up in this saying: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself."
verses.13:10: Love works no evil against a neighbor; therefore, love is the fulfillment of the law.
verses.13:11: And do this, knowing the time, that it is already the hour for you to awaken from sleep; for salvation is nearer to us now than when we first believed.
verses.13:12: The night has far advanced, and the day has drawn near. Let us therefore lay aside the deeds of darkness, and let us put on the armor of light.
verses.13:13: Let us walk properly as in the daytime, not in revelry and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and licentiousness, not in strife and jealousy.
verses.13:14: Rather, put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and do not make provision for the flesh concerning its desires.
verses.14:1: Now welcome the one who is weak in faith, not for disputes over opinions.
verses.14:2: One person has faith to eat all things, while the one who is weak eats vegetables.
verses.14:3: The one who eats must not despise the one who does not eat, and the one who does not eat must not judge the one who eats, for God has welcomed him.
verses.14:4: Who are you, judging another's household servant? To his own master he stands or falls; yet he will be made to stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand.
verses.14:5: One person judges one day above another, while another judges every day alike; let each one be fully convinced in his own mind.
verses.14:6: The one who observes the day observes it for the Lord. And the one who eats, eats for the Lord, for he gives thanks to God; and the one who does not eat, for the Lord he does not eat, and gives thanks to God.
verses.14:7: For none of us lives for himself, and no one dies for himself;
verses.14:8: for whether we live, we live for the Lord, or whether we die, we die for the Lord. Therefore, whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.
verses.14:9: For to this end Christ died and came to life, so that He might be Lord of both the dead and the living.
verses.14:10: But you, why do you judge your brother? Or you too, why do you despise your brother? For we will all stand before the judgment seat of God,
verses.14:11: for it is written, "As I live," says the Lord, "every knee will bow to Me, and every tongue will confess to God."
verses.14:12: So then, each one of us will give an account of himself to God.
verses.14:13: Therefore let us no longer judge one another, but rather decide this: not to place a stumbling block or a snare before a brother.
verses.14:14: I know and am convinced in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself; yet to the one who considers something to be unclean, to that person it is unclean.
verses.14:15: For if because of food your brother is grieved, you are no longer walking according to love. Do not by your food destroy that one for whom Christ died.
verses.14:16: Therefore do not let your good be spoken of as evil.
verses.14:17: For the kingdom of God does not consist in eating and drinking, but in righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit;
verses.14:18: for the one who serves Christ in this way is well-pleasing to God and approved by people.
verses.14:19: So then, let us pursue the things of peace and the things for building up one another.
verses.14:20: Do not tear down the work of God for the sake of food. All things indeed are clean, but it is wrong for the person who eats in a way that causes stumbling.
verses.14:21: It is good not to eat meat or drink wine or do anything by which your brother stumbles, or is tripped up, or is made weak.
verses.14:22: As for you, keep the faith that you have to yourself before God. Blessed is the one who does not judge himself in what he approves;
verses.14:23: but the one who doubts stands condemned if he eats, because it is not from faith; and everything that is not from faith is sin.
verses.15:1: Now we who are strong ought to bear the weaknesses of those without strength, and not to please ourselves.
verses.15:2: Let each one of us please his neighbor for what is good, toward building up;
verses.15:3: for Christ also did not please Himself, but just as it is written, "The insults of those who insult You fell upon Me."
verses.15:4: For whatever was written beforehand was written for our instruction, so that through endurance and through the encouragement of the Scriptures we might have hope.
verses.15:5: Now may the God of endurance and encouragement grant you to have the same mindset with one another according to Christ Jesus,
verses.15:6: so that with one accord, with one voice, you may glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.15:7: Therefore welcome one another, just as Christ also welcomed you, to the glory of God.
verses.15:8: For I say that Christ has become a servant of the circumcision on behalf of the truth of God, in order to confirm the promises to the fathers,
verses.15:9: and for the Gentiles to glorify God for His mercy; just as it is written, "For this reason I will give praise to You among the Gentiles, and to Your name I will sing praise."
verses.15:10: And again it says, "Rejoice, Gentiles, with His people."
verses.15:11: And again, "Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, and let all the peoples extol Him."
verses.15:12: And again Isaiah says, "There will be the root of Jesse, and the One who rises to rule over the Gentiles; in Him the Gentiles will hope."
verses.15:13: Now may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you believe, so that you may overflow with hope by the power of the Holy Spirit.
verses.15:14: Now I myself also am convinced about you, my brothers, that you yourselves are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, and able also to admonish one another.
verses.15:15: Yet I have written to you rather boldly on some points, as reminding you again, because of the grace given to me by God
verses.15:16: to be a minister of Christ Jesus to the Gentiles, performing priestly service with the gospel of God, so that the offering of the Gentiles may become acceptable, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.
verses.15:17: Therefore I have my boast in Christ Jesus in the things pertaining to God;
verses.15:18: for I will not dare to speak of anything except what Christ has accomplished through me for the obedience of the Gentiles, by word and deed,
verses.15:19: in the power of signs and wonders, in the power of the Spirit of God, so that from Jerusalem and all around as far as Illyricum I have fully proclaimed the gospel of Christ,
verses.15:20: and thus making it my ambition to proclaim the gospel not where Christ had been named, so that I might not build upon another's foundation,
verses.15:21: but just as it is written, "Those who were not told about Him will see, and those who have not heard will understand."
verses.15:22: For this reason also I have many times been hindered from coming to you.
verses.15:23: But now, having no longer any place in these regions, and having had a longing for many years to come to you,
verses.15:24: whenever I travel to Spain—for I hope while passing through to see you and to be sent on my way there by you, once I have first been satisfied in part with your company—
verses.15:25: but right now I am going to Jerusalem, serving the saints.
verses.15:26: For Macedonia and Achaia were pleased to make a contribution for the poor among the saints who are in Jerusalem.
verses.15:27: Indeed they were pleased to do so, and they are debtors to them; for if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual things, they are also obligated to serve them in material things.
verses.15:28: Therefore, when I have completed this and have sealed this fruit to them, I will set out by way of you for Spain.
verses.15:29: And I know that when I come to you, I will come in the fullness of the blessing of Christ.
verses.15:30: Now I urge you, brothers, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit, to strive together with me in prayers to God on my behalf,
verses.15:31: that I may be rescued from those who are disobedient in Judea, and that my service for Jerusalem may prove acceptable to the saints,
verses.15:32: so that I may come to you in joy through the will of God and be refreshed together with you.
verses.15:33: Now may the God of peace be with all of you. Amen.
verses.16:1: Now I commend to you Phoebe our sister, who is also a deacon of the church in Cenchreae,
verses.16:2: that you may receive her in the Lord in a manner worthy of the saints, and assist her in whatever matter she may have need of you; for she herself has also become a patron of many, and of myself as well.
verses.16:3: Greet Prisca and Aquila, my coworkers in Christ Jesus,
verses.16:4: who laid down their own necks for my life, to whom not only I give thanks, but also all the churches of the Gentiles,
verses.16:5: and the church in their house. Greet Epaenetus, my beloved, who is the firstfruit of Asia for Christ.
verses.16:6: Greet Mary, who labored much for you.
verses.16:7: Greet Andronicus and Junia, my relatives and my fellow prisoners, who are prominent among the apostles, who also were in Christ before me.
verses.16:8: Greet Ampliatus, my beloved in the Lord.
verses.16:9: Greet Urbanus, our coworker in Christ, and Stachys, my beloved.
verses.16:10: Greet Apelles, who is approved in Christ. Greet those of the household of Aristobulus.
verses.16:11: Greet Herodion, my relative. Greet those of the household of Narcissus who are in the Lord.
verses.16:12: Greet Tryphaena and Tryphosa, who labor in the Lord. Greet Persis, the beloved, who labored much in the Lord.
verses.16:13: Greet Rufus, chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.
verses.16:14: Greet Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas, and the brothers who are with them.
verses.16:15: Greet Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, and Olympas, and all the saints who are with them.
verses.16:16: Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the churches of Christ greet you.
verses.16:17: Now I urge you, brothers, to keep watch on those who cause divisions and stumbling blocks contrary to the teaching that you learned, and turn away from them;
verses.16:18: for such people do not serve our Lord Christ, but their own belly, and through smooth speech and flattery they deceive the hearts of the naive.
verses.16:19: For your obedience has reached everyone; therefore I rejoice over you, yet I want you to be wise as to what is good, and innocent as to what is evil.
verses.16:20: Now the God of peace will crush Satan under your feet soon. The grace of our Lord Jesus be with you.
verses.16:21: Timothy, my coworker, greets you, as do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my relatives.
verses.16:22: I, Tertius, who wrote the letter, greet you in the Lord.
verses.16:23: Gaius, host to me and to the whole church, greets you. Erastus, the treasurer of the city, greets you, and Quartus, the brother.
verses.16:24: ⟦The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.⟧
verses.16:25: Now to Him who is able to strengthen you according to my gospel and the proclamation of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery kept silent through eternal ages,
verses.16:26: but now manifested, and through the prophetic Scriptures, according to the command of the eternal God, made known to all the nations for the obedience of faith,
verses.16:27: to the only wise God, through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory forever. Amen!

notes.1:4: Greek horisthentos can mean 'designated,' 'appointed,' or 'declared.' The phrase 'Spirit of holiness' reflects a Semitic idiom and may refer to the Holy Spirit or to Christ's own spirit; 'by the resurrection of the dead' literally translates ex anastaseos nekron.
notes.1:17: The phrase 'from faith to faith' (ek pisteos eis pistin) is variously understood as 'by faith from start to finish,' 'from God's faithfulness to human faith,' or 'from one believer's faith to another.' In the Habakkuk 2:4 quotation, 'by faith' can modify either 'the righteous one' or 'will live.'
notes.1:28: Paul uses a Greek wordplay between edokimasan ('see fit' / 'approve') and adokimon ('depraved' / 'unfit' / 'disqualified').
notes.1:30: Greek theostygeis can be read actively ('God-haters') or passively ('hated by God').
notes.2:14: The adverb physei ('by nature') sits between clauses and may modify either 'who do not have the law' or 'do the things of the law.'
notes.2:16: The Greek verb krinei is accented as a present tense ('judges') in the critical text, though the same consonantal spelling can be accented as a future ('will judge').
notes.2:29: Greek en pneumati may refer either to the Holy Spirit ('by the Spirit') or to the inner human spirit ('in spirit'). Paul also alludes to the Hebrew name Judah (source of 'Jew'), which is linked to 'praise' (Genesis 29:35; 49:8).
notes.3:3: Paul plays on the cognates for faith and unfaithfulness here: the Greek terms rendered "proved unfaithful" and "unfaithfulness" can also mean "did not believe" and "unbelief," contrasting with the "faithfulness" of God.
notes.3:9: The Greek verb προεχόμεθα is debated: taken as a middle it asks "Are we at an advantage?" (or "Do we make excuses?"), whereas as a passive it asks "Are we at a disadvantage?" Similarly, οὐ πάντως can mean "Not at all" or "Not entirely."
notes.3:22: The Greek genitive phrase πίστεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ can be taken either objectively as "faith in Jesus Christ" or subjectively as "the faithfulness of Jesus Christ"; the same ambiguity recurs in 3:26.
notes.3:25: The Greek term ἱλαστήριον denotes a means of propitiation or atoning sacrifice, and in the Septuagint it specifically designates the mercy seat (atonement cover) on the ark of the covenant (Exod 25:17).
notes.4:1: The Greek phrase κατὰ σάρκα ("according to the flesh") can modify either "our forefather" or the verb "has found."
notes.4:19: While many later manuscripts read "he did not consider" (adding οὐ), the earliest witnesses omit the negative, indicating that Abraham realistically faced his and Sarah's condition without weakening in faith.
notes.4:25: Both clauses use the same Greek preposition διά with the accusative, expressing retrospective ground in the first ("because of our trespasses") and prospective purpose or result in the second ("for our justification").
notes.5:1: The Saints Greek Critical Text reads the hortatory subjunctive echōmen ("let us have"), supported by the earliest manuscripts, rather than the indicative echomen ("we have").
notes.5:6: The Greek text repeats eti ("still") before and after the participial phrase ("while we were still weak"), emphasizing human helplessness at the appointed time (kata kairon).
notes.5:12: The phrase eph ho is widely taken as causal ("because"), though some interpret it as "on the condition that" or "in whom"; Paul breaks off his comparison here and resumes it in 5:18.
notes.5:18: Both halves of the Greek comparison omit a main verb, concisely contrasting the universal result of Adam's trespass with that of Christ's act of righteousness.
notes.6:5: The adjective symphytoi literally means "grown together" or "planted together"; the second clause elliptically carries over "the likeness of" from the first.
notes.6:7: The verb dedikaiotai literally means "has been justified," here bearing the forensic sense of being acquitted or cleared from the claims of sin.
notes.6:13: Greek hopla can mean either "weapons" or "instruments"; "weapons" aligns with the chapter's imagery of reigning (6:12) and military wages (6:23).
notes.7:6: The text reads the plural participle apothanontes ("having died"), referring to believers rather than to the law; "Spirit" (pneumatos) contrasts the life-giving Spirit with the written letter.
notes.7:7: Greek epithymia ("coveting") and epithymeo ("covet") share the same root and carry the broader sense of desire (as in 6:12), specifically echoing the tenth commandment (Exod 20:17).
notes.7:14: Interpreters debate whether the first-person "I" of 7:14-25 depicts unredeemed humanity under the law, Israel under the Torah, or the believer's ongoing conflict with indwelling sin.
notes.7:21: The syntax of ton nomon is unusually compressed; commentators debate whether it means "this principle/rule" or refers to the Mosaic law itself.
notes.8:1: The Saints Greek Critical Text has the shorter reading ending at ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ ("in Christ Jesus"), without the later harmonizing addition from 8:4 ("who do not walk according to the flesh").
notes.8:2: The Saints Greek Critical Text reads the second-person singular pronoun σε ("you") rather than με ("me"), rendered literally as "freed you."
notes.8:3: περὶ ἁμαρτίας literally means "concerning sin" and is also the Septuagint idiom for a sin offering (as in Isa 53:10); keeping "concerning sin" leaves both senses open.
notes.8:10: πνεῦμα here could refer either to the believer's human spirit (rendered lowercase "spirit" to balance "the body") or to the Holy Spirit.
notes.8:11: The Saints Greek Critical Text uses the genitive διὰ τοῦ ἐνοικοῦντος αὐτοῦ Πνεύματος ("through His Spirit who dwells"), indicating agency, rather than the accusative variant ("because of His Spirit").
notes.8:15: Abba is the transliterated Aramaic term of intimate filial address, followed by the Greek articular vocative ὁ πατήρ ("Father"). υἱοθεσία literally means "placement as a son," rendered "adoption."
notes.8:26: ἀλαλήτοις literally means "wordless" or "unspoken" (groanings too deep for words). The Saints Greek Critical Text has the singular τῇ ἀσθενείᾳ ("our weakness") and no explicit ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν after ὑπερεντυγχάνει.
notes.8:28: In the Saints Greek Critical Text, ὁ θεός is not repeated as an explicit subject of συνεργεῖ. Taking πάντα as the neuter plural subject with a singular verb gives "all things work together toward good" (the alternative takes God as the implied subject: "He works all things together for good"). "His" before "purpose" is supplied from the context for κατὰ πρόθεσιν.
notes.8:34: The Saints Greek Critical Text reads Χριστὸς Ἰησοῦς ("Christ Jesus") and ἐγερθείς ("who was raised") without the later addition "from the dead."
notes.9:5: The punctuation of the final clause is debated; following the Greek punctuation here, "who is over all, God blessed forever" refers to Christ, though some punctuate it as an independent doxology to God the Father ("May God, who is over all, be blessed forever").
notes.9:22: Greek katertismena ("fitted" or "prepared") can be read as passive ("prepared") or middle/adjectival ("fit/ready for destruction"), contrasting with the active verb proetoimasen ("He prepared beforehand") in 9:23.
notes.9:28: Some later Greek manuscripts expand the quotation from Isaiah to read "in righteousness, because the Lord will carry out a shortened word upon the earth."
notes.9:29: "Sabaoth" is a Greek transliteration of the Hebrew title meaning "hosts" or "armies."
notes.10:4: Greek telos can mean either "end" (termination) or "goal" (culmination/purpose), and interpreters debate whether Paul intends one or both senses here.
notes.10:5: The critical Greek text reads en aute ("by it," referring to the righteousness from the law), whereas some manuscripts read en autois ("by them," referring to the things done).
notes.10:14: Literally "whom they have not heard," taking the genitive relative pronoun as the direct object of hearing.
notes.10:17: Greek akoe links 10:16 and 10:17 with a dual sense of "report/message" (10:16) and "hearing" (10:17); some later manuscripts read "the word of God" rather than "the word of Christ."
notes.11:4: Greek uses the feminine article with Baal ("the Baal"), reflecting the Septuagint convention of substituting the feminine noun aischyne ("shame") when reading Baal's name aloud.
notes.11:6: Later manuscripts add a symmetrical clause ("and if from works, it is no longer grace; otherwise work is no longer work"), which is absent from the earliest manuscripts.
notes.11:17: The Greek text reads three successive genitives ("of the root of the richness of the olive tree") without "and," whereas some manuscripts insert "and" ("of the root and of the richness").
notes.11:25: "In part" (apo merous) may refer to a partial hardening in extent (affecting part of Israel) or in duration, with the following "until" clause underscoring its temporary scope.
notes.11:31: The second "now" (nyn) is strongly attested in early manuscripts though omitted by some witnesses; the dative "because of the mercy shown to you" may alternatively modify the following clause ("so that by the mercy shown to you they also may now receive mercy").
notes.12:1: λογικὴν λατρείαν literally means "rational/reasonable cultic service" (also understood as "spiritual worship"); "rational service of worship" preserves both the philosophical sense of λογικός (engaging the mind, picked up in 12:2) and the sacrificial sense of λατρεία.
notes.12:2: The Saints Greek Critical Text reads τοῦ νοός ("the mind") without the possessive pronoun "your." δοκιμάζειν means to test and discern with approval; τέλειον means "complete" or "perfect."
notes.12:3: Paul uses a fourfold play on the root φρον- (ὑπερφρονεῖν, φρονεῖν, φρονεῖν, σωφρονεῖν), reflected by repeating "think" and closing with "sound judgment."
notes.12:8: ἁπλότης means "singleness of mind, simplicity," which in contexts of giving carries the nuance of ungrudging generosity.
notes.12:10: τῇ τιμῇ ἀλλήλους προηγούμενοι literally means "going ahead of one another in honor," rendered "in honor outdo one another."
notes.12:14: The Saints Greek Critical Text has τοὺς διώκοντας without "you" (ὑμᾶς), so it is rendered "those who persecute."
notes.12:16: τοῖς ταπεινοῖς can be masculine ("the lowly," i.e. humble people, rendered here) or neuter ("humble tasks/things"), contrasting with the neuter τὰ ὑψηλά ("high things").
notes.12:19: τῇ ὀργῇ ("to wrath") lacks a possessive pronoun in Greek; the context and the following Scripture quotation show it refers to God's wrath.
notes.13:1: Verses 1-2 feature a Greek wordplay on the root tasso ("order/arrange"): "submit" (hypotasso), "appointed" (tasso), "resists" (antitasso), and "ordinance" (diatage).
notes.13:9: Several later manuscripts add "You shall not bear false witness" to the list of commandments, but it is absent from the earliest witnesses.
notes.13:11: "The time" (kairos) denotes the decisive eschatological era rather than ordinary clock time, and the aorist "believed" points to when the readers first came to faith.
notes.14:1: The phrase "not for disputes over opinions" (Greek me eis diakriseis dialogismon) literally means "not for passing judgment on thoughts/opinions" and can refer either to avoiding quarrels over debatable matters or to refraining from judging the weak believer's scruples.
notes.14:13: Paul plays on two senses of the Greek verb krino: "let us no longer judge (krinomen) one another, but rather decide (krinate) this."
notes.14:14: "Unclean" translates Greek koinos (literally "common"), used in Jewish Greek to denote what is ritually defiled or profane.
notes.14:21: The Greek text here preserves the fuller wording "or is tripped up, or is made weak" (e skandalizetai e asthenei), which is omitted in several early manuscripts.
notes.15:9: Greek ethne means both "nations" and "Gentiles"; Paul links Old Testament passages about the nations (vv. 9-12) directly to his call to welcome Gentile believers.
notes.15:19: "Fully proclaimed" translates Greek peplerokenai (literally "fulfilled" or "completed"), referring to the completion of Paul's pioneer proclamation across the region.
notes.15:24: The Greek sentence breaks off here without completing its main clause (an anacoluthon) as Paul pivots in v. 25 to explain his immediate journey to Jerusalem.
notes.15:26: "Contribution" translates Greek koinonia (literally "fellowship" or "sharing"), portraying the relief collection for Jerusalem as an act of tangible partnership, echoed by the related verb "shared" (ekoinonesan) in v. 27.
notes.16:1: Greek diakonos can be rendered "deacon" or "servant"; similarly, prostatis in verse 2 refers to a "patron" or "benefactor."
notes.16:7: Greek episemoi en tois apostolois is debated and may mean either "prominent among the apostles" (as part of them) or "well known to the apostles."
notes.16:24: This verse is enclosed in double brackets because it is absent from the earliest and most reliable manuscripts, appearing to be a later scribal addition.
notes.16:25: The closing doxology (16:25-27) is positioned at different places in ancient manuscripts (after 14:23, after 15:33, or at the end of the letter); this text prints it here and also, in double brackets, after 14:23.

unplaced.text: ⟦Now to Him who is able to strengthen you according to my gospel and the proclamation of Jesus Christ, according to the revelation of the mystery kept silent through eternal ages,⟧
unplaced.note: Text-critical double brackets ⟦ ⟧ are preserved from the Saints Greek Critical Text; some Greek manuscripts place this doxology at the end of chapter 14 rather than 16:25-27.

⟦to the only wise God, through Jesus Christ, to whom be the glory forever. Amen.⟧
